metadata.title: Erdafitinib: FGFR3-selected urothelial treatment
metadata.indication: Unresectable/metastatic urothelial carcinoma with susceptible FGFR3 alteration after at least one PD1/PDL1-containing line in that setting.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.

contexts.duration_text: Continuous treatment until progression or unacceptable toxicity;28 days is a reference view.

metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Source reconciliation draft; independent clinical approval pending
encoding_maturity.scope_note: The phosphate input is explicitly mg/dL to preserve printed source thresholds. Do not enter Irish mmol/L results into it; verify units and conversion with pharmacy. Rounded source mmol/L values differ at some boundaries. Source dose ladder9→8→6→5→4→stop, or8→6→5→4→stop; no further dose reduction below4 mg. Baseline eye examination; monthly for first4 months then every3 months; urgent assessment of new visual symptoms. Phosphate day 14–21 and monthly thereafter, more often when raised. Avoid vitaminD supplementation unless the oncology team specifically resolves the phosphate/calcium concern. Review grapefruit/Seville oranges, interacting medicines and QT risk.

source_boundary_notes: The phosphate input is explicitly mg/dL to preserve printed source thresholds. Do not enter Irish mmol/L results into it; verify units and conversion with pharmacy. Rounded source mmol/L values differ at some boundaries.
Source dose ladder9→8→6→5→4→stop, or8→6→5→4→stop; no further dose reduction below4 mg.
Baseline eye examination; monthly for first4 months then every3 months; urgent assessment of new visual symptoms. Phosphate day 14–21 and monthly thereafter, more often when raised.
Avoid vitaminD supplementation unless the oncology team specifically resolves the phosphate/calcium concern. Review grapefruit/Seville oranges, interacting medicines and QT risk.

action.message: Source: continue current dose with prescribed phosphate binder with food until phosphate <7. Sustained elevation/associated toxicity may require reduction. Assess duration and other abnormalities.

action.message: Withhold until phosphate <7; test weekly and start prescribed binder. Same-dose restart requires review; ≥9 for one month or linked toxicity requires reduction.

action.message: Withhold until phosphate <7; weekly testing and medical management; restart one dose level lower only after review. Persistent ≥10 for >2 weeks has a permanent-stop rule.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Highest emetogenic active component and phase-specific NCCP classification.
premedication: Confirm the tablet strength, daily dose, early phosphate appointment and baseline eye examination before starting.
other_support: High phosphate may need a dietitian-guided phosphate restriction and prescribed phosphate binder. Do not add vitaminD supplements without oncology review. Ask about mouth care, skin/nail care, diarrhoea treatment and dry-eye support. Bring all medicines and supplements for interaction checking.
